messages:
aria: FYI — we're seeing degraded GPU capacity in ap-southeast-1 starting ~06:12 UTC. Autoscaler began shifting traffic out; some requests landed in cpu-backup and quantized variants. Opening this thread to capture runbook updates and immediate action items.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-214 created for ap-southeast-1 capacity degradation. Incident page: https://redwood/incident/INC-2026-214
max: Quick check: NVLINK/ECC errors on node g-aps-17 and g-aps-18. 12/24 GPUs reported ECC warnings, several pods evicted. Logs: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors --format=csv` shows spikes.
sanjay: Network fabric flaps (ib0) correlate with pod evictions. Likely upstream switch causing packet drops and node reboots.
tara: Side effect: traffic-shift policy sent traffic to quantized model variants in us-west-2, which caused p99 latency to spike and a small quality regression for some prompts. We need guardrails.
lee: Observed that the current failover policy only checks aggregate capacity and not variant compatibility. It allowed a cross-region shift to a different model family. Fallback/variant selection logic needs to prefer same-family equivalents first.
aria: Proposed runbook updates (high level):
1) Pre-failover validation: verify both network path health and target pool variant compatibility.
2) Dry-run mode: shift 5% traffic for 2 minutes and validate latency & quality before full shift.
3) Automated rollback triggers: p99 latency threshold and eval-set quality signal.
4) Cost guardrail: warn on estimated egress increase > 25% and notify finance.
aria: Adding a quick check snippet to the runbook for ops oncall to run before manual/auto shift:
```\n# run from control-plane (example)\nrcli nodes list --region ap-southeast-1 --filter "gpu_ecc>0"\nrcli pool metrics get --pool gpu-primary --region ap-southeast-1 --window 5m\n# verify network path to candidate region\nnetdiag traceroute --to us-west-2.redwood.internal --proto tcp --port 443 --max-hops 12\n# check variant compatibility\nrcli models compare-compat --src gpt-4a --dst gpt-4a-quant --check-ops=kvcache,attn\n```
max: Suggest adding an automated compatibility check in the routing layer: if compatibility_score < 0.9, don't route unless operator overrides. Also add telemetry to show which variant was chosen during shift.
tara: For rollback thresholds: propose immediate rollback if p99 latency > 500ms for 5m OR eval-set BLEU/ROUGE/QA metric drops by > 1 relative point in dry-run. Those thresholds can be tuned but should exist.
sanjay: Add a network pre-check step to the playbook that runs systematic TCP/UDP test suites and validates path MTU and retransmit rates. If packet loss > 0.5% on control plane or >1% on data plane, abort shift.
lee: Cost / procurement note — cross-region shifts may trigger expensive egress. Add a budget check: if estimated egress for shift > $X/day (placeholder), require approval from billing@. Also add a step to publish an alert to #finance-alerts channel.
oncall-jess: I'll create the PR to docs/runbooks/apac-failover.md with the above snippets and a new section 'pre-failover validation' and tag eng-sre for review. ETA: 48h.
ops-bot: Action items added to INC-2026-214: 
- aria: verify nvlink replacement schedule and node remediation (48h)
- max: add compatibility check to routing layer + telemetry (72h)
- sanjay: add network diagnostics & threshold tests to runbook (48h)
- lee: add billing guardrail and finance alert flow (48h)
ops-bot: Status: oncall acknowledged, assignees notified.
aria: Additional note for the runbook: include a 'fail-open' vs 'fail-closed' decision matrix. Some customers prefer latency over quality, others prefer quality. Document how to choose per customer SLO.
max: Also add a 'chaos' validation in staging to exercise cross-region shifts weekly so we know regressions early.
tara: Good call. I'll prepare a small eval suite with 200 canonical prompts to run during a dry-run. Keep it lightweight.
aria: OK — next steps: PR for runbook (oncall-jess), routing change proposal (max), network checks (sanjay), billing guardrail (lee). We'll reconvene in incident postmortem to fold any additional learnings into the playbook. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
